mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline > 1% MoM does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% MoM does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary cycle, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% YoY, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and GDPC1 growth < 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of HOUST decline > 10% YoY and GDPC1 growth < 2% YoY does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a quarter, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5% in a quarter does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.
